text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- A mourning China takes an hour off to pay respects to Deng Xiaoping during memorial ceremony at which President Jiang Zemin pledges continuity to mentor's policies.
- Top financial officials from U.S. and five key Pacific Rim economies, including Singapore, to meet in Tokyo next Tuesday to launch a forum that may evolve into an Asian G-6.
- Two explosions blow up buses in Urumqi, capital of China's mainly Muslim region of Xinjiang.

- Courts will not deal with Ecstacy abusers lightly, even if offender is tertiary student, because that would send wrong signal to other students, chief justice says in jailing polytechnic student for six months.
- A 150,000 square foot area, about half Malaysian high commissioner's disused residence at Gallop Road, will be up for sale soon.
- International panel of top business leaders suggests Singapore develop world-class businesses by promoting climate of entrepreneurship and cautions against over-regulation.
- Singapore Power wants to use existing underground national cable network to offer full range of multimedia services as well as basic telephone service for which it's bidding.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- Banks warned to watch out for nearly US$250 million worth of fraudulent letters of credit and guarantees floating around financial market.
Economists revise first quarter and full year growth forecasts up a notch to five percent and 7.1 percent respectively.
- U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers has moved Asian foreign exchange operations from Singapore to Tokyo.
- Concerns over corporate profits and recent downweighting of Singapore market in Morgan Stanley Capital Index pull Straits Times Industrials Index down 1.4 percent.
- Some building contractors turn down new residential jobs, wary of getting into cashflow problems should developers stall on payments in a slow residential property market.
- Listed department stores look poised for brighter days as yet another operator, Robinson, reports better-than-expected interim results.
- Diversified Hwa Hong Corp raising Singapore $38.4 million through private placement of 14.6 million new shares.
- Genting Bhd reports flat set of final results which saw lower contributions from its main money-spinner casino in second-half 1996.
- United International Securities announces slightly higher earnings of S$7.7 million and warns of inflationary pressures building in the United States.
- Industrial hardware maker Sin Soon Huat posts 30 percent rise in interim net earnings to S$6.2 million thanks to strong regional sales.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
